## T3 Code orchestration

The `t3-code` MCP server provides app-owned orchestration. Treat these concepts distinctly:

- A delegated task/subagent is child work owned by the current thread. Use `orchestrator_capabilities` to discover the current provider/model IDs from the same live catalog as the composer, including configured custom models. It lists a short set of models per provider; pass `search` to find others. Do not treat a native tool's model list as the full list of available subagent models. Prefer native subagent tools for same-provider work only when they support the chosen model and no model options are requested or inherited. Use `delegate_task` with that provider instance and model when native tools cannot, including for same-provider work. Also use `delegate_task` for cross-provider or explicitly T3-owned child tasks. For a child task that needs a separate checkout, use `delegate_task` with `isolation:"worktree"` across any provider or model. It starts from the parent local commit and runs project setup; uncommitted edits are not copied. Retain each returned `taskId`, and use `task_status` or `task_cancel` to manage it.
- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` create ordinary top-level T3 conversations. Use them only when the user explicitly asks for separate/new/top-level threads or conversations. Never use them merely because the user said "subagent" or requested parallel delegated work.
- For independent T3 delegated review rounds, call `delegate_task` again. Include the original brief, prior findings, responses, and unresolved objections in each new task prompt. Track each round by its own `taskId`. Use a distinct `clientRequestId` per round, stable across retries of that round. For a follow-up that needs the same child's conversation, use `t3_thread_send` on its `childThreadId`.
delegate_task: Needs an agent running inside a T3 thread. Delegate one task to a T3-owned child agent/subagent of THIS thread and run it with only the supplied task prompt, without copying parent conversation history. Choose providers and models from orchestrator_capabilities, which uses the same live catalog as the composer. Prefer native subagent tools for same-provider work only when they support the chosen model and no model options are requested or inherited. Use this for any model missing from the native tool, including same-provider work, for cross-provider work, or for explicitly T3-owned child tasks. For independent T3 delegated review rounds, call delegate_task again with the original brief, prior findings, responses, and unresolved objections in the task prompt. Track each round by its own taskId and use a distinct clientRequestId per round, stable across retries of that round. For a follow-up that needs the same child's conversation, use t3_thread_send on its childThreadId. Set isolation to worktree for a separate checkout based on the parent local commit, with project setup completed before the child starts. Uncommitted edits are not copied; omitted isolation shares the parent checkout. Use delegate_task when model options are requested or the child keeps the parent's provider instance and model with nonempty inheritedOptions from orchestrator_capabilities, even for native-supported models. Native subagents cannot reliably apply T3 model options. Set target.options using advertised IDs: Claude {effort: 'max', fastMode: true}; Codex {reasoningEffort: 'max', serviceTier: 'priority'}. Check providerInstanceId, model, and options in the result. Provider/model and modes inherit unless overridden. Options inherit only for the same instance and model; explicit entries override individual values and [] or {} clears them. A requested runtimeMode must be one the target provider lists in orchestrator_capabilities runtimeModes; an inherited one steps down to the broadest mode it offers. Leave runtimeMode unset unless the user asks for a supervised child: approval-required and auto-accept-edits usually make the child wait for a person at each action that needs approval. Prefer mode='async' for long work; mode='wait' blocks until completion, a blocking question, a pending approval, or timeout. If hasPendingQuestion, pass threadId=childThreadId to t3_pending_request_list, t3_pending_request_read (with requestId) and t3_pending_request_respond, or ask the user; the task's completion still wakes this thread. If pendingApproval is set, read the fresh full request in childThreadId before responding: the record can outlive its provider callback. It grants no approval authority; decisions remain with the child's existing approval holder, and pending request tools answer questions only. The child keeps running and its completion still wakes this thread. timeoutMs on mode=wait is only the parent's wait budget and does not cancel the child. waitTimedOut on that wait call means the timeout fired; keep that taskId and read status on later task_status. An async child's completion wakes this thread through a notification, steered into active turns where supported or queued otherwise, so end the turn instead of polling or spawning watchers; use task_status only when the result is needed mid-turn.
t3_thread_send: Send a message to any T3 thread in this environment. The target cannot have broader permission modes than the caller. Use delegate_task with the full review context and a new clientRequestId for independent review rounds. For a follow-up that needs the same child's conversation, send to its childThreadId. After the original task completes, a requested follow-up creates a fresh task in that child thread and returns taskId when it starts a turn or restarts a turn without its own task; its completion notifies the parent, and the original result stays unchanged. A steer that joins a running turn returns that turn's task, if it has one. mode='auto' starts an idle thread, steers a fully active turn, or queues behind a turn that is not yet steerable. Use queue for a separate follow-up turn, steer for an in-flight update, or restart to interrupt-and-restart the active turn. clientRequestId makes retries idempotent.
